correctness.rationale: For every real or complex 1<p<infinity and both weights, phase alignment reduces the spatial radius to a compact positive-variable maximization. With both weights positive, a positive optimizer is interior by perturbing x or z from zero; quotient stationarity leads to one explicit strictly decreasing root, implying the full exact formula. Boundary and zero-weight cases follow by continuity or one-link optimization. The complex range is a closed disk by rotation symmetry and connected modulus; the real range is an interval. The p=4 strict ordering follows algebraically from two cubics, a unique positive root, and a factored strictly positive polynomial. The standalone local verifier replayed 2694 checks including reconstructed stationary witnesses and exponent-reversal identities; finite testing supplements but is not the proof.

originality.rationale: The 2022 An--Heo Example 2.4 gives exactly the one-edge Banach-space constant, hence covers either coordinate axis but does not determine interaction of two adjacent nonzero weights. Gau--Wu 2014 and Undrakh et al. 2015 treat Hilbert spatial numerical radii, yielding the p=2 special case but not the mixed-exponent characterization, conjugate-exponent reversal, or quartic ordering for p=4. Chang--Wang 2012 concerns Hilbert weight permutations. Earlier own-ledger local first derivative at p=2 cannot imply all-p exact norm or ordering. Searches of published-finding corpus and relevant primary literature did not locate the full claim; unresolved old Banach numerical-range literature is disclosed as a real residual risk, not treated as proof from silence.

value.rationale: This is the complete exact numerical radius for a natural, irreducible-at-positive-weights two-parameter 3-coordinate nilpotent shift family, the first finite path with interacting adjacent weights. The resulting Banach-space operator invariant is a mixed-p-and-q Luxemburg coefficient norm, not the Euclidean Hilbert invariant; it determines every coefficient radius, extremizing directions, complete numerical range, conjugate-exponent reversal, and a provable strict quartic order-sensitivity. These structural consequences provide the nontrivial motivation beyond routine substitution of known one-edge cases.
